xmldoc.short_description: Create an event table for a timetable.

param_input_item.param_description: Datetime or duration vector containing event start times.
Timetable whose row times become event times and whose variables become event variables.
Event labels. A scalar value is expanded to all events.
Duration values that specify event lengths.
Datetime or duration values that specify event end times.
Name or index of a variable of the input timetable that stores event labels, lengths, or end times. Only valid when the first input is a timetable.

param_output_item.param_description: Event table: a timetable whose row times are the event times.

description.p: eventtable creates an event table that can be attached to a timetable through Properties.Events; syncevents then copies its variables into the timetable.

When the input is a time vector, event labels, lengths, and end times are specified with name-value arguments. Additional event variables are supplied by first creating a timetable and then passing that timetable to eventtable: any positional input after the first one is an error.
An event table is a timetable: the event times are its row times (E.Properties.RowTimes, or E.Time), not a variable, so size, width, indexing and concatenation behave as for a timetable.

E.Properties starts with EventLabelsVariable, EventLengthsVariable and EventEndsVariable, the names of the variables holding the event labels, lengths and end times ([] when unset). They can be assigned a variable name or index, or []. A variable renamed or removed is unset.

Created from event times without labels, the event table gets the labels "Event 1", "Event 2", ... in an EventLabels variable. Created from a timetable, no variable is used as labels unless specified.
